articles.title: Strange radio signals from space could come from a dead star
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: The night sky is as good a place as any for a mystery. Back in 2002, astronomer Scott Hyman and his colleagues detected five mysterious bursts of radio waves coming from near the center of our galaxy, spaced roughly 77 minutes apart. The signals were detected again in 2003 and 2004, but then disappeared. Despite years of searching, there was no sign of their return.

articles.title: Researchers review isotope methods for tracing and quantifying gaseous nitrogen production in soils
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Researchers from the Institute of Applied Ecology (IAE) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have reviewed stable nitrogen isotope techniques for tracing the sources and quantifying the production of gaseous nitrogen in soils. The review examines four approaches for distinguishing microbial pathways that produce nitrous oxide (N₂O), nitric oxide (NO) and dinitrogen (N₂).

articles.title: Stem cell–derived nanoparticles modulate immune cells and help delay type 1 diabetes in mice
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: In people with type 1 diabetes, the immune system mistakenly identifies insulin-producing cells in the pancreas as foreign and attacks them, leaving the body unable to properly regulate blood sugar. While insulin therapy helps manage the disease, it does not stop the underlying immune attack.

articles.title: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why
articles.summary: Scientists may have finally explained why up to more than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from rocks around the world. New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological history before they were buried and preserved.
